brief: September nonfarm payrolls rose 29k, below the 90k consensus and down from a downwardly revised 133k in August (itself cut from 162k). The 3-month payroll average stands at 51k and the 12-month average at 41k, both still above the breakeven pace needed to hold unemployment steady, so Natixis reads the slowdown as normalization of an existing trend rather than new deterioration. The unemployment rate edged up to 4.175% (rounding to 4.2%) from 4.141% as participation rose from 61.6% to 61.8%, which Natixis calls a positive sign rather than labor-market weakening. Wage growth cooled to 0.1% m/m / 3.0% y/y (13bps m/m), keeping the labor market from adding any inflationary impulse. Natixis says the data does not change the Fed's broader calculus since inflation remains the supreme concern, but it lowers the urgency to hike in October and possibly December. The bank still expects fewer hikes this cycle than the market is pricing, forecasting only one more rate increase.
